title: Chopin on an Érard and a modern recording
work: Étude in E minor, Op. 25 No. 5
question: How do Goldstein’s 1851 Érard and Neeman’s modern recording shape the étude’s contrasting touches?
intro: Martha Goldstein plays an Érard dated 1851, while Edward Neeman’s recording belongs to Musopen’s Set Chopin Free project. Goldstein’s session date is unknown: the instrument’s age does not date the performance. The planned Pachmann transfer is omitted because its source imposes a non-commercial licence.
